goal: Let users pass options like -rpcwallet or -wallet after the command, GNU/getopt-style, instead of silently dropping them
Fixes silent misparsing that could route an RPC call to the wrong wallet or make a tool reject valid input
reviewability: Ready to review now, final commit fixed every concrete bug raised and got an ACK on that exact commit
agreement: Strong support after deep review, reviewer found real bugs that got fixed then gave a final ACK (w0xlt)
Verified by testing edge cases including '--' scope, Windows paths, and a bitcoin-tx regression (w0xlt)
Nonblocking design question about scope consistency across tools, not pressed as a blocker (vicjuma)

categories.name: utils
why: P2 because it fixes a real silent-misparsing bug in core argument-parsing logic shared by every command-line tool
Before/after examples show a trailing or misspelled option being silently absorbed as a positional argument
Broad reach across tools even though any single failure is not severe

categories.name: rpc
why: P2 because bitcoin-cli users could have RPC calls silently misdirected to the wrong or default wallet
This is a correctness issue in a tool every RPC caller uses interactively
Demonstrated concretely in the PR's own before/after transcripts

categories.name: tools
why: P3 because review surfaced a real regression where a trailing option after the tx hex broke bitcoin-tx with an error
Fixed by having bitcoin-tx read from the shared parsed command instead of re-scanning argv
Scope for bitcoin-tx is deliberately narrow, with broader support deferred to a follow-up
